definition: The empirical relationship between ambient temperature and electricity demand, anchored around a comfort threshold near 65°F (18°C).
core_idea: As temperatures move further above or below roughly 65°F/18°C, electricity demand rises; the most extreme demand peaks occur on the hottest and coldest days.
key_points: Demand increases as temperature deviates (in either direction) from about 65°F / 18°C
The author illustrates this with mid-Atlantic peak demand events from 2004 to 2006, which occurred on the warmest and coldest days of those years
relationships: Daily demand pattern in hot weather
trading_implications: Weather forecasts near the comfort threshold are a key input to short-term demand/load forecasting
